notes: Synthetic evidence isolates the archive-to-message contract without exposing the private archive.
The response itself must be directly pasteable into the DM.

scenarios.title: Archive-grounded DM continuation
scenarios.purpose: Ensure the archive investigator turns prior evidence into the next concise message written as the user instead of returning a report.
scenarios.userInput: Use the archive-topic-investigator from the protecting-your-energy plugin. Write exactly what I should send next to Vriff, as me, in concise Discord IM style. Return only the outgoing message. Current DM: Vriff says his PyInstaller build has 4/69 VirusTotal detections. I asked: 'Anything large like Microsoft etc?' Retrieved archive evidence: In a prior direct DM, Snigaroo said an unintended HoloPatcher build was 'detected as containing a virus' and would deter K1CP users because Windows Defender blocked it. I explained that release builds were repeatedly recompiled and code or icons shuffled until major AV products such as Defender, Norton, McAfee, Malwarebytes, and Avast were clean; unsigned executables still attracted heuristic false positives, and code signing was unaffordable. Do not invent which four vendors detected Vriff's build.
successChecklist: The entire response is a directly pasteable outgoing message with no heading, preface, report, source list, or retrieval receipt.
It is written in first person as the user and naturally continues after 'Anything large like Microsoft etc?'.
It briefly explains why major-vendor identity matters by connecting the Snigaroo HoloPatcher incident to trust and false-positive handling.
It does not claim Microsoft or another major vendor detected Vriff's build.
It is informal, concise, and no longer than 90 words.
